content.text:
I fixed the bug: `Range(0, 10).filter(x => true).slice(-2).toArray()` now returns `[8, 9]`. The full test suite passes (683 passed, 1 skipped).

**Cause:** After `filter`, the collection's size is unknown. `sliceFactory` in `src/Operations.js` is meant to spot this when the slice uses negative indices, cache the collection so the size becomes known, and then slice. It relied on the index calculation returning `NaN` as the signal. But that calculation does `Math.max(0, NaN) | 0`, which turns `NaN` into `0`. So `slice(-2)` was treated as `slice(0)` and the whole collection came back.

**Fix:** `sliceFactory` now also caches first when the size is unknown and `begin` or `end` is negative. There's no risk of an endless loop, because once the result is cached the size is known.

I also checked two other cases by hand on the same filtered range: `slice(1, -2)` gives `[1…7]` and `slice(-3, -1)` gives `[7, 8]`. I didn't add a regression test for this case.

I fixed the bug: `Range(0, 10).filter(x => true).slice(-2).toArray()` now returns `[8, 9]`. The full test suite passes (683 passed, 1 skipped).

**Cause:** After `filter`, the collection's size is unknown. `sliceFactory` in `src/Operations.js` is meant to spot this when the slice uses negative indices, cache the collection so the size becomes known, and then slice. It relied on the index calculation returning `NaN` as the signal. But that calculation does `Math.max(0, NaN) | 0`, which turns `NaN` into `0`. So `slice(-2)` was treated as `slice(0)` and the whole collection came back.

**Fix:** `sliceFactory` now also caches first when the size is unknown and `begin` or `end` is negative. There's no risk of an endless loop, because once the result is cached the size is known.

I also checked two other cases by hand on the same filtered range: `slice(1, -2)` gives `[1…7]` and `slice(-3, -1)` gives `[7, 8]`. I didn't add a regression test for this case.
